newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WILLIAMS HOMERS TWICE TO LEAD YANKS PAST TWINS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WILLIAMS HOMERS TWICE TO LEAD YANKS PAST TWINS.

text.p: Just two days after coming off a lengthy stay on the disabled list with a hamstring injury, Bernie Williams hit two homers and drove in four runs on Sunday to lead the New York Yankees to a 6-5 victory over the Minnesota Twins.
Williams, who was activated Friday, went 7-for-11 with three home runs and six RBI in three games against the Twins.
"He's a big part of our offence and defence," said Yankee outfielder Paul O'Neill. "It's hard to come off the disabled list and hit like the way he's hit."
Williams hit a solo homer in the fourth inning and blasted a three-run homer in the fifth off Latroy Hawkins as the Yanks built a 6-2 lead en route to their fifth win in six games.

Dwight Gooden (5-3) pitched five-plus innings and allowed three runs and five hits to earn the win. Mariano Rivera yielded a run in the ninth, but picked up his league-best 32nd save. Hawkins (3-7) lasted four-plus innings and surrendered six runs and eight hits.

After Chuck Knoblauch pulled the Twins within 3-2 with an RBI double in the fifth, Derek Jeter and Wade Boggs singled in the bottom of the inning and Williams followed with his three-run shot to right as the Yankees pulled away.
In Oakland, Harold Baines capped a three-run seventh inning with a two-run homer and B.J. Surhoff had two doubles and a pair of RBI as the Baltimore Orioles rallied for a 7-5 win over the Athletics.
Baines's 13th home run off T.J. Mathews (1-1) put the Orioles in front 7-4 and they went on to win for the 11th time in their last 13 games.
Shawn Boskie (6-4) pitched two scoreless innings for the victory in relief of starter Rick Krivda. Randy Myers picked up his 31st save in 32 opportunities.
In Milwaukee, Jay Buhner and Lee Tinsley drove in two runs each in a four-run fifth inning and Randy Johnson notched his 15th win as the Seattle Mariners held on for a 6-5 victory over the Brewers.
Buhner doubled home two runs to erase a 3-2 deficit and scored along with Edgar Martinez on a triple by Tinsley.

The rally provided a 6-3 lead for Johnson (15-3), who allowed three runs and four hits in six innings. The revamped Mariners bullpen made it interesting as Mike Timlin allowed a two-run homer by Jeromy Burnitz in the eighth.
In Kansas City, Mike Macfarlane homered twice and Ricky Bones allowed six hits over seven innings as the Royals continued their dominance of the Boston Red Sox with a 5-2 victory.
Jay Bell and Yamil Benitez added solo homers for the Royals, who are 7-1 against Boston this season.
Macfarlane tied the game 1-1 in the third and gave the Royals a 4-2 lead with a two-run blast in the seventh off Tim Wakefield (5-13), who leads the major leagues in losses.
Reggie Jefferson hit a pair of homers for the Red Sox.

In Detroit, Willie Blair allowed one earned run in six-plus innings for his seventh straight win and Travis Fryman homered and drove in two runs as the Tigers posted a 5-2 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays.
Blair (11-4) gave up eight hits with no walks and two strikeouts. The right-hander, who began his career with Toronto, has not lost since June 22.
Bob Hamelin and Melvin Nieves also homered off Toronto starter Woody Williams (6-10), who surrendering all five runs and seven hits in 6 1/3 innings.
In Anaheim, Chuck Finley allowed one run over eight innings to win his eighth straight start as the Angels beat the Chicago White Sox 4-1 for their seventh win in eight games.

Finley (11-6) gave up five hits while walking three and striking out four. Chicago's James Baldwin (7-12) yielded three runs and five hits over seven innings, walking five and striking out two in losing his third straight start.
Tim Salmon and Dave Hollins had solo homers for the Angels, who scored single runs in the last four innings.
At Texas, Will Clark's sacrifice fly scored Tom Goodwin with the winning run as the Rangers rallied for three runs in the bottom of the ninth to defeat the Cleveland Indians 8-7.

Cleveland closer Mike Jackson (2-3) loaded the bases in the ninth and Mark McLemore's two-run double tied the game before Clark's shallow flyball scored Goodwin just ahead of centre fielder Marquis Grissom's throw.
Benji Gil hit a two-run homer and Gonzalez added a solo shot for the Rangers.
John Wetteland (6-2) got the victory, despite allowing a run in the ninth.
